title: Briefing: France, India, Albania, Canada and Italy
script: This is the Unowned briefing for Monday, November second. It's narrated by a synthetic voice, and every fact comes from our checked timelines.
Every item carries our grade. Confirmed means independent outlets agree. Reported means only one source has it so far. Disputed means the accounts conflict. And alleged is one side's claim.

France. From October twenty-seventh: French student and pupil organisations say the government's October twenty-sixth education measures fall short and vow to keep mobilising, AFP reports. Our grade: reported. LCP and La Dernière Heure have it, but we can't yet count them as independent confirmation.

India. From October thirty-first: Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke said the party backs the INDIA bloc's November first Ramlila Maidan rally against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar but will not take part, calling the CJP "a neutral platform", Hindustan Times. We grade that confirmed: Hindustan Times and Outlook India reported it independently.

Albania. From October twenty-eighth: Albania's government has presented its 2027 tax package, dropping an earlier plan to raise corporate income tax, cutting VAT on 54 basic foods from 20% to 6% while raising the standard rate to 21%. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, Tirana Times, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

Canada. From October thirtieth: Imperial Oil's chief executive said he is encouraged by progress toward a binding Pathways carbon-storage agreement with Ottawa and Alberta, a condition for the Pacific Link pipeline, though "there's still a lot of work left to do," BNN Bloomberg reports. We grade that reported: so far only BNN Bloomberg has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.

Italy. From October thirtieth: Tens of thousands marched in Rome, Milan and other Italian cities on Friday against the cost of living and military spending, NBC News reports, as the USB union and others called public- and private-sector strikes. Our grade: reported. It rests on one source, NBC News, and isn't yet confirmed by a second.

France's high school protests. From October twenty-sixth: The government announces it will cancel the 836 secondary-education post cuts planned in the 2027 budget and add 500 teaching posts in public lycées, AFP reports via La Dernière Heure and LCP. We grade that reported: La Dernière Heure and LCP carry it, but we haven't yet established that their reporting is independent.

The Cockroach Janta Party movement. From October thirty-first: Cockroach Janta Party president Abhijeet Dipke posted an Instagram note to singer Diljit Dosanjh saying he was hurt by the singer's June comments on the protests and asking to end the row, News18, Hindustan Times and The Tribune report. Our grade: confirmed, with independent reporting from Hindustan Times and News18.

Albania's student protests. From October twenty-eighth: Tirana’s Chamber of Commerce and Industry and Pro Export Albania oppose the government’s proposed 2027 fiscal package, which the Albanian Daily News says would raise dividend tax from 8% to 15% and tourism VAT from 6% to 10%; it also cites a corporate income tax rise to 17%, which Tirana Times reports was dropped before the package was formally presented on October twenty-eighth. We grade that reported: so far only Albanian Daily News has it, and we're waiting for independent confirmation.

Canada's Pacific Link pipeline fight. From October twenty-sixth: Carney, most premiers and Assembly of First Nations leaders held their first such meeting since 2005; Carney said ministers will work with First Nations on moving beyond the Indian Act. Our grade: reported. CP24 and Turtle Island News have it, but we can't yet count them as independent confirmation.
Coming up in the days ahead. November fourth, South Africa: local government elections on November fourth.
That's the briefing. Full timelines, and every source, are at unowned news dot com.
